The thicker shielding means lower dB loss. 240 grade is .24 inches thick, while .400 is ~.40 inches thick. 400 has less loss. For length up to 15 foot, 240 is more than adequate, but for 25 or 50 foot length, the 400 is recommended. The cable can be used to put an extension between an SMA antenna connector on a LoRa device or Meshtastic radio and an N-female antenna. Compare gain loss of this cable at 6ft example length: 915 MHz application: - 0.4 dB (LoRa device) Compare this to a cheaper RG-58 shielded cable of the same length- the gain loss would be -0.9 dB for 915 MHz. Twice as much loss with inferior cable!
